html:
From May to October 1917 three shepherd children at Fátima in central Portugal said that the Virgin Mary appeared to them on the 13th of each month. Fátima became one of the largest Catholic pilgrimage sites in the world.

The children, Lúcia, Francisco and Jacinta, told of messages calling for prayer and penance and of secrets about war and Russia. On 13 October a large crowd reported seeing the sun dance in the sky, the Miracle of the Sun. The church approved the apparitions in 1930.

The cult grew during the anticlerical First Republic and was embraced by the regime of Salazar. Millions of pilgrims visit each year, and several popes have come. The two younger children were declared saints in 2017. See Portugal and the Catholic Church.
